newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan ministry to probe role in oil dealer scandal.
newsitem.headline: Japan ministry to probe role in oil dealer scandal.

text.p: Japan's trade minister said on Tuesday he has instructed his ministry to conduct an internal investigation over a scandal involving ties with an oil dealer arrested of tax evasion.

"I have instructed that an investigation be conducted within the ministry of our people's relations with (Junichi) Izui, and to make public the result of the investigation," Trade Minister Shinji Sato told a news conference.
Millionaire oil wholesaler Junichi Izui has boasted of his close ties with high-ranking politicians and bureaucrats and has allegedly wined and dined many of them.

Izui, who was arrested earlier in the month on charges he evaded 310 million yen ($2.76 million) in taxes, also made political donations to numerous politicians, including key ministers of Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's government.

Local media reported that the oil trader made hefty profits in a series of deals with giant oil companies, and the Ministry of International Trade and Industry, which is in charge of the oil industry, was under fire for Izui's alleged ties with high-ranking MITI bureaucrats.

Sato said some 100 high-ranking officials and department heads of his ministry, including those who have worked in the Petroleum Department of the Agency of Natural Resources and Energy, an arm of MITI, will be questioned.
The minister's secretariat will lead the probe, "but I will personally select the people whom I trust" to conduct the investigation, Sato said.
MITI's move comes amid public outcry over a series of misconduct allegations against bureaucrats, from excessive wining and dining to outright bribery.
On Monday, the governor of Akita Prefecture in northern Japan said he would resign to take responsibility for massive misuse of taxpayers' money by government bureaucrats.
